newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish PM expected to win no-confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Swedish PM expected to win no-confidence vote.

text.p: Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson will face a vote of confidence in parliament on Friday following opposition criticism of his policy on China.
Social Democrat Persson has come under sharp criticism for remarks he made about China's political system during an official visit to Beijing this month.
Political commentators said the Swedish premier was expected to survive the vote easily.
The parliament, or Riksdag, will begin the vote at 0800 GMT, a parliamentary spokeswoman said.
The three opposition parties -- the Conservatives, Liberals and Christian Democrats -- which filed the no-confidence motion together have 121 seats in the 349-member Lower House.
The Green Party said its 27 members would abstain from the vote, while the ruling Social Democrats and non-government Centre and Leftist parties, together numbering 201, said they would back Persson.

The opposition pressed for the vote after Persson failed to retract the disputed comments at a meeting on Wednesday of Sweden's foreign affairs advisory council. He also failed to withdraw the comments during an emergency parliamentary debate.
Persson told Swedish businessmen in Beijing: "To me, it's striking what political stability means for economic development when you look at the Chinese example."

His opponents accused Persson of giving comfort to China's hard line on political dissent. The prime minister described the criticism as exaggerated and said he had not implied any positive judgement in the phrase "political stability."
